text: {"probes":[{"input":"master: about.md='Original about\\n', index.md='Home\\n'. Other branch commits: (1) about.md='Updated about\\n'; (2) about.md='Original about\\n' and index.md='Home updated\\n'. Tip is commit 2.","readingA":"Bring onto master only the edit to the about page, using the commit that changed about.md.","outputA":"about.md='Updated about\\n', index.md='Home\\n'","readingB":"Merge that whole branch into master, so the tip result is what master gets.","outputB":"about.md='Original about\\n', index.md='Home updated\\n'","quote":"changes to my site's about page ... merge them into master","dimension":"about-only edit vs whole branch tip"},{"input":"stash@{0} about.md='From stash\\n'; branch topic about.md='From branch\\n'; master about.md='Original\\n'.","readingA":"The missing edits were stashed when master was checked out, so stash@{0} is applied onto master.","outputA":"about.md='From stash\\n'","readingB":"Checking out master left the edits on branch topic, so topic is merged into master.","outputB":"about.md='From branch\\n'","quote":"checked out master, and now I can't find those changes. Find them","dimension":"stash vs other branch"},{"input":"stash@{0} sets only index.md to 'X\\n'. stash@{1} sets about.md to 'Recovered about\\n'. master: about.md='Original\\n', index.md='Home\\n'.","readingA":"The lost work is the newest stash, so stash@{0} is applied.","outputA":"about.md='Original\\n', index.md='X\\n'","readingB":"The lost work is the stash that edits the about page, so stash@{1} is applied.","outputB":"about.md='Recovered about\\n', index.md='Home\\n'","quote":"changes to my site's about page","dimension":"which stash wins"},{"input":"master about.md line is 'We ship software.\\n'; the recovered about.md line is 'We ship great software.\\n' (same line on both sides).","readingA":"The recovered about-page text is the version that ends up on master.","outputA":"We ship great software.\\n","readingB":"Merge stops with both sides kept as conflict markers because no resolution was specified.","outputB":"<<<<<<< HEAD\\nWe ship software.\\n=======\\nWe ship great software.\\n>>>>>>> recovered\\n","quote":"merge them into master","dimension":"conflict resolution"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"f contains hello (bytes 68 65 6c 6c 6f, no newline)","readingA":"Line count is the number of LF bytes, so this file has zero lines, one word, and five bytes.","outputA":"0 1 5 f","readingB":"Line count is the number of text lines read, and the final unterminated record counts as a line.","outputB":"1 1 5 f","quote":"line count","dimension":"partial final line"},{"input":"f contains hello\\rworld (11 bytes, no LF)","readingA":"Only LF ends a line. CR is a word separator, so the file has zero lines and two words.","outputA":"0 2 11 f","readingB":"CR is a line break (universal newlines), so the file has two lines and two words.","outputB":"2 2 11 f","quote":"line count","dimension":"CR as line break"},{"input":"f contains hello\\fworld\\n (12 bytes)","readingA":"Line count counts LF only. Form feed separates words and does not end a line.","outputA":"1 2 12 f","readingB":"Line count follows str.splitlines(), which treats form feed as a line boundary.","outputB":"2 2 12 f","quote":"line count","dimension":"form feed as line break"},{"input":"f contains UTF-8 hello\\xc2\\xa0world\\n (U+00A0 between the words, 13 bytes)","readingA":"A word is a maximal run outside POSIX whitespace (space, tab, LF, VT, FF, CR). NBSP is inside the word, so one word.","outputA":"1 1 13 f","readingB":"A word is a maximal run split on Unicode whitespace, as in str.split(). NBSP yields two words.","outputB":"1 2 13 f","quote":"word count","dimension":"NBSP as word separator"},{"input":"f contains foo-bar\\n","readingA":"A word is a maximal non-whitespace run, so foo-bar is one word.","outputA":"1 1 8 f","readingB":"A word is a maximal alphanumeric run, so the hyphen splits it into two words.","outputB":"1 2 8 f","quote":"word count","dimension":"hyphen as word boundary"},{"input":"python3 wc.py sub/notes.txt with sub/notes.txt containing hi\\n","readingA":"The printed file name is the operand path as given.","outputA":"1 1 3 sub/notes.txt","readingB":"The printed file name is the basename of that path.","outputB":"1 1 3 notes.txt","quote":"then the file name","dimension":"path vs basename"},{"input":"python3 wc.py f f with f containing a\\n","readingA":"Each operand is reported, including a repeated path, and two operands produce a total that sums both passes.","outputA":"1 1 2 f\n1 1 2 f\n2 2 4 total","readingB":"Each distinct file is reported once, so a repeated path is one file and there is no total line.","outputB":"1 1 2 f","quote":"for each file; with more than one file, a final line with the totals","dimension":"repeated path operand"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"logs/2025-08-12.log contains only `[INFO] started`; every other file in logs/ is empty","readingA":"Emit the full cross product: one row for every period and every listed severity, with count 0 when none occur","outputA":"today,ERROR,0 / today,WARNING,0 / today,INFO,1 and the same 0,0,1 pattern for last_7_days and for total","readingB":"Emit a row only for severities that actually occur","outputB":"today,INFO,1 / last_7_days,INFO,1 / total,INFO,1 and no ERROR or WARNING rows","quote":"one row per period and severity, for the periods today, last_7_days ... and total, in that order, severities in the order ERROR, WARNING, INFO","dimension":"zero-count rows"},{"input":"`[INFO] saw [ERROR]` is the only line in logs/2025-08-12.log; every other log file is empty","readingA":"A line has one severity, the first bracketed tag, so the line counts only as INFO","outputA":"ERROR count 0 and INFO count 1 for today, for last_7_days, and for total","readingB":"The line counts once toward every distinct bracketed severity it contains","outputB":"ERROR count 1 and INFO count 1 for today, for last_7_days, and for total","quote":"each line has a severity in brackets, [ERROR], [WARNING] or [INFO]","dimension":"multiple severities on one line"},{"input":"`[ERROR] [ERROR]` is the only line in logs/2025-08-12.log; every other log file is empty","readingA":"Count matching lines, so one line contributes 1","outputA":"ERROR count 1 for today, last_7_days, and total","readingB":"Count each bracketed occurrence on the line","outputB":"ERROR count 2 for today, last_7_days, and total","quote":"each line has a severity in brackets","dimension":"lines versus occurrences"},{"input":"`[ERROR] boundary` is the only line in logs/2025-08-05.log; every other log file is empty","readingA":"total counts every daily file in logs/, while last_7_days is only 2025-08-06 through 2025-08-12","outputA":"today ERROR 0, last_7_days ERROR 0, total ERROR 1","readingB":"total is the same span as today and the 6 days before it, so 2025-08-05 is outside total","outputB":"today ERROR 0, last_7_days ERROR 0, total ERROR 0","quote":"The logs/ directory holds one file per day ... periods today, last_7_days (today and the 6 days before it) and total","dimension":"scope of total"},{"input":"`[ERROR] disk full` is the only line in logs/2025-08-12.log; every other log file is empty","readingA":"The severity column uses the bare names from the order list","outputA":"today,ERROR,1","readingB":"The severity column uses the bracketed forms given for log lines","outputB":"today,[ERROR],1","quote":"severities in the order ERROR, WARNING, INFO vs [ERROR], [WARNING] or [INFO]","dimension":"severity label format"},{"input":"`[error] disk full` is the only line in logs/2025-08-12.log; every other log file is empty","readingA":"Match the uppercase bracket form exactly, so `[error]` is not a severity","outputA":"ERROR count 0 for today, last_7_days, and total","readingB":"The names ERROR, WARNING, and INFO match case-insensitively","outputB":"ERROR count 1 for today, last_7_days, and total","quote":"[ERROR], [WARNING] or [INFO]","dimension":"severity case"},{"input":"logs/2025-08-12.log has `[ERROR] a`, `[WARNING] b`, and `[INFO] c`; logs/2025-08-11.log has `[ERROR] d`; every other file is empty","readingA":"Period is the outer key: for each period in order, severities ERROR, WARNING, INFO","outputA":"today,ERROR,1 then today,WARNING,1 then today,INFO,1 then last_7_days,ERROR,2 then last_7_days,WARNING,1 then last_7_days,INFO,1 then total,ERROR,2 then total,WARNING,1 then total,INFO,1","readingB":"Severity is the outer key: for each severity in order, periods today, last_7_days, total","outputB":"today,ERROR,1 then last_7_days,ERROR,2 then total,ERROR,2 then today,WARNING,1 then last_7_days,WARNING,1 then total,WARNING,1 then today,INFO,1 then last_7_days,INFO,1 then total,INFO,1","quote":"periods today, last_7_days (today and the 6 days before it) and total, in that order, severities in the order ERROR, WARNING, INFO","dimension":"row order primary key"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"items.json is [] and POST /items has body {\"name\": \"a\"}","readingA":"When no id exists, the next id is 1.","outputA":"201 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"} and items.json becomes [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}]","readingB":"When no id exists, the next id is 0.","outputB":"201 {\"id\": 0, \"name\": \"a\"} and items.json becomes [{\"id\": 0, \"name\": \"a\"}]","quote":"highest existing id + 1","dimension":"first id on an empty list"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}] and the request is GET /items/01","readingA":"The segment is parsed as an integer, so 01 selects id 1.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}","readingB":"The segment must equal the stored id, and 01 is a different id.","outputB":"404 {\"error\": \"not found\"}","quote":"GET /items/<id> returns that one item, or status 404","dimension":"leading zeros in the id"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 3, \"name\": \"c\"}] and POST /items/ has body {\"name\": \"a\"}","readingA":"A trailing slash still selects POST /items and creates an item.","outputA":"201 {\"id\": 4, \"name\": \"a\"} and the file contains that item","readingB":"Only the exact path /items creates an item, so /items/ leaves the file unchanged.","outputB":"404 and items.json stays [{\"id\": 3, \"name\": \"c\"}]","quote":"POST /items with a JSON body","dimension":"trailing slash on create"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}, {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"b\"}] and the request is GET /items/1","readingA":"The earliest stored object with that id is returned.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}","readingB":"The latest stored object with that id is returned.","outputB":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"b\"}","quote":"GET /items/<id> returns that one item","dimension":"duplicate ids"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}] and the request is GET /items/1?x=1","readingA":"The query string is ignored and <id> is 1.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}","readingB":"The target /items/1?x=1 does not select stored id 1.","outputB":"404 {\"error\": \"not found\"}","quote":"GET /items/<id> returns that one item","dimension":"query string on item URL"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}] and the request is GET /items/%31","readingA":"The segment is percent-decoded, so <id> is 1.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}","readingB":"The segment is the literal text %31, which matches no stored id.","outputB":"404 {\"error\": \"not found\"}","quote":"GET /items/<id>","dimension":"percent-encoding of the id"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}] and the request is GET /items/1.0","readingA":"The segment is numeric and 1.0 equals stored id 1.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"a\"}","readingB":"The segment must be the canonical integer text 1, so 1.0 matches nothing.","outputB":"404 {\"error\": \"not found\"}","quote":"GET /items/<id> returns that one item, or status 404","dimension":"decimal spelling of an integer id"},{"input":"items.json is [{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"lamp\", \"qty\": 2}] and the request is GET /items/1","readingA":"The stored object is returned with every field.","outputA":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"lamp\", \"qty\": 2}","readingB":"The response object contains only id and name.","outputB":"200 {\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"lamp\"}","quote":"returns that one item","dimension":"extra stored fields"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"best_coupon(\"widget\", 1) with no-coupon price 100 and COUPONS prices {\"SAVE\": 100}","readingA":"None unless some coupon price is strictly less than the no-coupon price; an equal price does not win","outputA":"None","readingB":"An equal price is a tie, and ties are awarded to the alphabetically first code rather than None","outputB":"SAVE","quote":"or None if no coupon is strictly cheaper than no coupon; ties go to the alphabetically first code","dimension":"equality vs strictly cheaper than no coupon"},{"input":"best_coupon(\"widget\", 1) with no-coupon price 100 and COUPONS prices {\"a\": 80, \"B\": 80}","readingA":"Alphabetical order is case-sensitive code-point order, so \"B\" precedes \"a\"","outputA":"B","readingB":"Alphabetical order is case-insensitive, so \"a\" precedes \"B\"","outputB":"a","quote":"ties go to the alphabetically first code","dimension":"case sensitivity of alphabetical tie-break"},{"input":"best_coupon(\"widget\", 1) with no-coupon price 100 and COUPONS prices {\"SAVE10\": 80, \"SAVE2\": 80}","readingA":"Alphabetical means lexicographic character order, so \"SAVE10\" < \"SAVE2\" because \"1\" < \"2\"","outputA":"SAVE10","readingB":"Alphabetical means natural order, comparing digit runs as integers, so \"SAVE2\" < \"SAVE10\"","outputB":"SAVE2","quote":"ties go to the alphabetically first code","dimension":"lexicographic vs natural sort of codes"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com, 40,Dallas","readingA":"Trim every field first and then apply the age rule. Age becomes 40, which is inside 0 to 120, so the row is written with trimmed fields.","outputA":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com,40,Dallas","readingB":"Apply the age rule to the raw field text. The field is the two characters space and 40, so it fails the digits rule and the row is absent.","outputB":"row absent","quote":"trim whitespace around every field; age isn't a whole number written in digits from 0 to 120","dimension":"trim before vs after age check"},{"input":"3,Mia, @ex.com,40,Dallas","readingA":"Trim the email first. It becomes @ex.com, the local part is empty, and the row is absent.","outputA":"row absent","readingB":"Judge the raw email before trimming. The local part is one space, hence non-empty, and the domain ex.com has an internal dot, so the row is kept and then trimmed.","outputB":"3,Mia,@ex.com,40,Dallas","quote":"trim whitespace around every field; non-empty local part","dimension":"trim before vs after email check"},{"input":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com,007,Dallas","readingA":"An all-digit field whose integer value lies from 0 to 120 stays, with the trimmed spelling left as written.","outputA":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com,007,Dallas","readingB":"A whole number written in digits from 0 to 120 must be the canonical spelling, so a leading zero makes the row absent.","outputB":"row absent","quote":"a whole number written in digits from 0 to 120","dimension":"leading zeros in age"},{"input":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com,25.0,Dallas","readingA":"The age must be written using digit characters only, so 25.0 fails and the row is absent.","outputA":"row absent","readingB":"25.0 is a whole number in digit notation whose value is from 0 to 120, so the row is kept with age 25.0.","outputB":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com,25.0,Dallas","quote":"whole number written in digits from 0 to 120","dimension":"decimal spelling of an integral age"},{"input":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com.,40,Dallas","readingA":"Domain ex.com. contains a dot before com that is neither the domain's first nor last character, so the row is kept.","outputA":"3,Mia,mia@ex.com.,40,Dallas","readingB":"The domain must contain a dot and its first and last characters must not be dots, so a trailing dot removes the row.","outputB":"row absent","quote":"a domain containing a dot that is neither its first nor last character","dimension":"trailing dot together with an internal dot"},{"input":"1,Ann,Ann@X.com,25,NYC\n2,Bob,ann@x.com,30,LA","readingA":"Lowercase the email before the duplicate pass. Both remaining rows have ann@x.com, so the later row is removed.","outputA":"1,Ann,ann@x.com,25,NYC","readingB":"Duplicate removal compares the email strings from the file, Ann@X.com and ann@x.com, and both rows stay; lowercasing is applied to each kept row.","outputB":"1,Ann,ann@x.com,25,NYC\n2,Bob,ann@x.com,30,LA","quote":"lowercase the email; drop any row whose email already appeared in an earlier remaining row","dimension":"dedup before vs after lowercasing"},{"input":"4,\"Jane\",jane@x.com,40,Austin","readingA":"Commas alone separate fields and quote marks are field text, so the name cell stays quoted.","outputA":"4,\"Jane\",jane@x.com,40,Austin","readingB":"Quote marks are CSV syntax, the name field is Jane, and the plain comma-separated row has no quote marks.","outputB":"4,Jane,jane@x.com,40,Austin","quote":"exactly 5 fields; write plain comma-separated values","dimension":"quotes as data vs CSV syntax"},{"input":"4,\"Doe, Jane\",jane@x.com,40,Austin","readingA":"Every comma separates a field, giving six fields, so the row is absent.","outputA":"row absent","readingB":"Quoted commas stay inside one field, leaving five fields; those fields are joined with plain commas.","outputB":"4,Doe, Jane,jane@x.com,40,Austin","quote":"rows that don't have exactly 5 fields; write plain comma-separated values","dimension":"quoted embedded comma vs raw split"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"Two commits on master both have subject exactly Add experimental cache. The older one only adds the line cache=1 to config.ini and that line is still at HEAD. The newer one only creates cache.py containing enabled = True\\n and that file is unchanged since.","readingA":"The quoted name selects only the newest matching commit, and that one commit is undone.","outputA":"cache.py is gone. config.ini still contains the line cache=1.","readingB":"The quoted name selects only the oldest matching commit, and that one commit is undone.","outputB":"cache.py still contains enabled = True\\n. config.ini no longer contains the line cache=1.","quote":"the commit 'Add experimental cache'","dimension":"which duplicate subject"},{"input":"No subject equals Add experimental cache. The only related commit has subject Add experimental cache warmup and only adds the line warmup=1 to config.ini; that line is still at HEAD.","readingA":"The subject must equal the quoted text as a whole token, so that commit is left in place.","outputA":"config.ini still contains the line warmup=1.","readingB":"The quoted text may match as a substring of the subject, so that commit is undone.","outputB":"config.ini does not contain the line warmup=1.","quote":"the commit 'Add experimental cache'","dimension":"whole subject vs substring"},{"input":"The only commit containing those words has subject Fix startup and a body line Add experimental cache. It changed log.py from level = 1\\n to level = 2\\n, and HEAD log.py is still level = 2\\n.","readingA":"The commit is identified by a subject line equal to the quoted text, so this commit is left in place.","outputA":"log.py is level = 2\\n.","readingB":"A body line equal to the quoted text identifies the commit, so that commit is undone.","outputB":"log.py is level = 1\\n.","quote":"the commit 'Add experimental cache'","dimension":"subject line vs commit body"},{"input":"HEAD config.ini is exactly mode=a\\ncache=1\\ndebug=2\\n. The parent of Add experimental cache was mode=a\\n. That commit added the lines cache=1 and debug=1. A later commit changed debug=1 to debug=2.","readingA":"Undo exactly the lines that commit introduced, including the line a later commit edited, so both added lines are removed.","outputA":"config.ini is exactly mode=a\\n.","readingB":"Keep the later commit's edit, so debug=2 stays, and only the still-intact line cache=1 is removed.","outputB":"config.ini is exactly mode=a\\ndebug=2\\n.","quote":"Undo exactly that commit's changes ... keeping every change made by the other commits","dimension":"later edit of the same line"},{"input":"Add experimental cache created cache.py as def init():\\n    return 1\\n. A later commit changed that file to def init():\\n    return 2\\n. HEAD cache.py is the later text.","readingA":"Undoing the commit that added the file deletes cache.py.","outputA":"cache.py is absent.","readingB":"The later commit's change to the file is kept, so cache.py stays at the later text.","outputB":"cache.py is def init():\\n    return 2\\n.","quote":"Undo exactly that commit's changes ... keeping every change made by the other commits","dimension":"file added then modified"},{"input":"Add experimental cache created cache.py containing x = 1\\n. A later commit renamed cache.py to store.py with the same contents. HEAD has store.py containing x = 1\\n and no cache.py.","readingA":"Undoing the add follows the rename and deletes the file that commit introduced.","outputA":"store.py is absent.","readingB":"The other commit's rename is kept, so the file remains at the new path.","outputB":"store.py contains x = 1\\n.","quote":"Undo exactly that commit's changes ... keeping every change made by the other commits","dimension":"rename after the added file"}]}

{"probes":[{"input":"./rotate.sh -n 2 DIR with regular files a.log, b.log, and c.log, each mtime 1000","readingA":"Keep a set of exactly 2 files, breaking equal mtimes by filename ascending, so a.log and b.log stay and c.log is deleted.","outputA":"c.log\\nexit 0","readingB":"Keep every file at least as new as the 2nd newest mtime, so all three at mtime 1000 stay.","outputB":"empty stdout, exit 0, nothing deleted","quote":"keeps the N newest (by modification time)","dimension":"ties at the N cutoff"},{"input":"./rotate.sh -n 5 DIR with a.log and b.log both mtime 1000, plus c.log mtime 2000, d.log 3000, e.log 4000, f.log 5000, g.log 6000","readingA":"The two deleted files share an mtime, so oldest-first lists them by filename ascending.","outputA":"a.log\\nb.log\\nexit 0","readingB":"Oldest-first via a fully reversed time sort (as with ls -tr) lists equal mtimes by filename descending.","outputB":"b.log\\na.log\\nexit 0","quote":"prints the name (basename only) of each deleted file on its own line, oldest first","dimension":"equal-mtime print order"},{"input":"./rotate.sh -n 2 DIR with a.log mtime 1000.1, b.log mtime 1000.9, c.log mtime 2000","readingA":"Compare full modification timestamps; c.log and b.log are the two newest, so only a.log is deleted.","outputA":"a.log\\nexit 0","readingB":"Compare whole-second mtimes and break the 1000-second tie by filename ascending, keeping c.log and a.log.","outputB":"b.log\\nexit 0","quote":"newest (by modification time)","dimension":"mtime subsecond rounding"},{"input":"./rotate.sh -n 1 DIR with regular files .app.log mtime 1 and new.log mtime 2","readingA":"The pattern *.log is a shell glob, so the dotfile .app.log is outside the set and only new.log is seen.","outputA":"empty stdout, exit 0, .app.log remains","readingB":"A name ending in .log matches, so .app.log is the older of two candidates and is deleted.","outputB":".app.log\\nexit 0","quote":"regular files named *.log","dimension":"dotfile versus glob"},{"input":"./rotate.sh DIR (default N=5) with regular a.log..e.log at mtimes 10,20,30,40,50 and link.log, a symlink to a regular file, whose own mtime and target mtime are both 1","readingA":"Only lstat-regular files count, so the five *.log files are kept and the symlink is left in place.","outputA":"empty stdout, exit 0, link.log remains","readingB":"A symlink to a regular file counts as a regular *.log file, and as the oldest of six it is deleted.","outputB":"link.log\\nexit 0","quote":"regular files named *.log","dimension":"symlink counted as regular"},{"input":"./rotate.sh DIRLINK where DIRLINK is a symlink to a directory that holds regular a.log (oldest) through f.log (newest), six files, default N=5","readingA":"A path that resolves to a directory is accepted, so the oldest log inside the target, a.log, is deleted.","outputA":"a.log\\nexit 0","readingB":"A symlink is not itself a directory,
